model: I = a*b_hat + s*G_hat, a,s >= 0. b_hat is the LOCAL material chromaticity from an alpha-aware opening; G_hat is the illuminant, measured from the plate.

corneal_glints.clipping_note: a clipped glint has no diffuse underneath to recover; subtraction leaves a flat patch there and this stage reports it rather than filling it

cross_check.why_it_matters: the two estimators share no pixels and no mechanism, so agreement is real cross-validation rather than one metric confirming itself

window.why_face_scaled: a constant pixel radius is wrong on at least two of: a 1080p bust, a 6K anamorphic macro close-up, a wide shot

floor.why: skin gets MORE saturated as it darkens (subsurface reddening), which mimics the dichromatic specular signature. Measured over 58819 cheek pixels of one material, min/sum spans 0.060 (p2) to 0.216 (p95). Ungated, the separator reads that drift as specular and desaturates the whole face to grey-green.
floor.consequence: the low-level sheen below the floor stays in the diffuse layer and is relit as if it were diffuse. That is a real ceiling on constraint 5, not a tuning choice.

identity: D = plate - s*G_hat. Every diffuse pixel is a plate pixel minus a scalar times a measured colour; no generative model is in the path (constraint 15).
limits: cannot recover texture under a CLIPPED highlight -- none was recorded there
near-neutral materials (a white shirt, grey foam, metal) are unseparable by ANY dichromatic method; see mean_unseparable_fraction
the sub-floor sheen on skin is not separable from a single unpolarised image
on V-Log footage this MUST run after the decode (constraint 18)
